title: I Forwarded the Wedding Seating App After They Sold My Table

parts.text: I opened the seating app at 4:19 p.m. the day before the wedding and my table of high-school friends was now a corporate sponsor booth. I had RSVP'd in March. I was thirty-one, bridesmaid-adjacent, holding a dyeable shoe. The couple texted that sponsors pay for flowers. I screenshotted my RSVP, the old table, and the new booth. Then I forwarded the app link to both sets of parents who were still listed as hosts. At 4:27 the bride called me crying that I had involved her mother.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Her mother has the app link and the sponsor booth where my March RSVP sat.

social.video_title: They sold the high-school table to a sponsor booth — Part 1/2
social.description: March RSVP, dyeable shoe, flowers argument. Parents were hosts. Would you have sat with a logo?

parts.text: The parents unsold the booth. We sat at table 8 with people I knew. Flowers were already paid for, it turned out, by a different line item. I danced. The app had a history tab, which is a mean gift. Sponsors got a sign by the bar. High school got chicken. Involving hosts is what hosts are for. I dyed the shoe a color that photographed well next to no logo.

social.video_title: The history tab unsold the booth — Part 2/2
social.description: Table 8 restored, bar sign for sponsors, chicken. Was a flower a friend?
